title: A Group Chat for the Mixtape
premise: Coral Vasquez, seventeen, has spent years perfecting the art of being fine—cooking dinner, signing permission slips, and keeping his siblings' struggles off every radar while their mother works hospital night shifts. When his AP English teacher assigns a college essay on 'the question nobody can stop answering,' Coral writes about a fire at Rivera Middle School that the district quietly blamed on faulty wiring—and discovers his little sister's asthma diagnosis and three other families' illnesses line up with buried water contamination reports. As he builds an underground group chat of affected students to gather testimony before the school board's budget vote destroys the evidence, Coral must choose between the scholarship essay that could free him from his family's survival math and the exposure that could blow their fragile life apart. He publishes everything the night before the vote, loses the scholarship interview but wins a state investigation, and learns that belonging sometimes means burning your own exit door.
about_author: Oscar Nakamura is a former after-school program coordinator who grew up translating parent-teacher conferences for his neighbors in a working-class coastal town. He writes stories about kids who hold families together with duct tape and stubbornness.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A chaotic morning—burnt eggs, Marisol's forgotten inhaler refill, a permission slip forged in Mom's handwriting—establishes the Vasquez household's delicate machinery. At school, Coral is the invisible kid who teachers praise for 'resilience.' Emotional beat: the exhausting pride of carrying a family no one sees carrying you.

chapters.title: The Question Nobody Can Stop Answering
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Ms. Okafor assigns the college essay prompt: 'What truth does your community avoid?' Coral plans to write something safe and forgettable, but when Marisol has an asthma attack during dinner, he starts listing dates in his notebook—every flare-up mapped against the semester the middle school pipes were replaced. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Records Request, Denied
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A public records request returns forty pages, half redacted, including a 2019 environmental consultant's report with its conclusion blacked out. The librarian, Mr. Ferro, quietly slips him the name of a retired custodian who 'kept copies of things.' Emotional beat: the first vertigo of knowing something adults don't want known.

chapters.title: The Custodian's Boxes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Coral and Ray Delgado, the retired custodian, who shows Coral water test results showing solvent contamination and a memo ordering them shredded. Ray's hands shake—not from age, from guilt. Emotional beat: inherited responsibility; Coral realizes silence was a decision someone made, and he can unmake it.

chapters.title: A Group Chat for the Mixtape
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral starts an anonymous group chat with four classmates whose siblings got sick, naming it after the mixtape playlist they share to cope. They compare timelines, hospital bills, and a fifth name: a board member's nephew who attended Rivera. Emotional beat: the electric relief of not being the only one awake at 3 a.m.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Interview
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Coral and Priya (a chat member). Coral's full-ride interview goes well until he deflects a question about 'challenges' and realizes the safe essay he submitted is a lie of omission. Meanwhile the district announces a facilities consolidation vote that would seal the old Rivera records permanently. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: What Mom Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Mom's POV, one rare day shift. She notices Coral's burnout, the forged signature, the notebook left open. Instead of confronting him, she tells him about the factory job she lost for reporting safety violations—the origin of her own silence. Emotional beat: love expressed as warning; duty as both inheritance and cage.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A chat member's parent, a district employee, finds the chat and threatens expulsion and legal action. One member quits; another's testimony gets subpoenaed prematurely. The board votes to move the consolidation vote up by two weeks. Emotional beat: betrayal and panic—the machine pushing back.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Vote
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral drafts two essays: the safe scholarship one and the true one. With his siblings asleep, he uploads the consultant report, the memo, and recorded testimonies to a local journalist, then submits the true essay to Ms. Okafor and the scholarship committee. Emotional beat: quiet terror becoming resolve; the match striking.

chapters.title: Louder Than Fine
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The story breaks; the vote collapses amid jeers and a state investigation announcement. Coral loses the scholarship but gains a journalism mentorship and a district-funded health screening program—Marisol's inhaler finally covered. The group chat renames itself after the victory. Emotional beat: grief and triumph braided together; belonging won at real cost.
